essenceNote: Kenya's foreign languages at Grade 9 are Arabic, French, German, and Mandarin — each a non-formal, basic (A1/YCT2-equivalent) 4-skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing) curriculum, taught in parallel structure across all four languages per the shared essence statement.

notes: Uniquely among Grade 9 subjects built so far, the same 9 themes (Greetings, Family, Countryside, Time, Fun/Plans, Food, Body/Health, Weather/Environment, Getting Around) repeat identically across all 3 strands — each strand teaches the theme's vocabulary through a different modality (oral interaction vs written comprehension vs guided writing/spelling), per the curriculum's own per-theme SLO wording (a/b/c bullets differ by strand type even when the theme and much of the vocabulary is shared). Per the standing 'never merge sub-strands' rule, this still means 27 distinct skills (9 themes x 3 strands), not 9 — but each strand's skill is built to test its theme through that strand's actual modality (LS = oral vocabulary/expression recall, R = short French passage + comprehension, W = spelling/gap-fill/word-order) rather than being a copy-pasted repeat of the same exercise, so the 3 skills per theme are not redundant.
